src: Shipwrecks hand-checked against NOAA, US Navy NHHC, Parks Canada, Institute of Nautical Archaeology, Mary Rose Trust, Vasa Museum, Western Australian Museum, UNESCO, national heritage and accident investigation bodies; each entry names its sources. Positions marked approximate are within about 20 km.
fmt: [year, ship, lat, lon, kind, lives lost (lower figure), lives lost text, depth m, year found or raised, found note, fact, Wikipedia title, sources, sinking event title, found event title, 1 if position approximate]
w: found by sponge diver Mehmet Çakır; excavated 1984-1994 by the Institute of Nautical Archaeology

A Late Bronze Age merchant ship that sank off Kaş, Turkey, around 1320 BCE carrying about ten tons of copper ingots plus tin, glass and luxury goods. It is the richest Bronze Age cargo found in the Mediterranean, evidence of trade between the Levant, Cyprus, Egypt and the Aegean.
A Bronze Age trader sinks off Uluburun with ten tons of copper
The Uluburun Bronze Age wreck is found off Turkey
found by sponge diver Kemal Aras; excavated 1960 by George Bass for the Penn Museum

A small Late Bronze Age ship carrying copper and tin ingots that sank off Cape Gelidonya, southern Turkey, around 1200 BCE. Its 1960 excavation was the first ancient shipwreck fully excavated on the seabed by archaeologists.
A Bronze Age metal trader sinks off Cape Gelidonya
Archaeologists dig the Cape Gelidonya wreck: the first full excavation on the seabed
found by diver Andreas Cariolou; excavated 1968-1969; now in Kyrenia Castle

A small Greek merchant ship that sank about a nautical mile off Kyrenia, Cyprus, around 294 BCE with wine jars and almonds. Its well-preserved hull shows how ancient Greek ships were built shell-first and repaired.
A Greek merchant ship sinks off Kyrenia, Cyprus
found by Greek sponge divers; salvaged 1907-1913; finds in the Bardo Museum, Tunis
A Roman-era ship carrying Greek bronze and marble sculpture and furniture that sank about 5 km off Mahdia, Tunisia, around 80-70 BCE. It is a major source on the Hellenistic art trade.
French Ministry of Culture (DRASSM); Oxford Roman Economy Project
A ship of Greek art sinks off Mahdia
found by French Navy divers; excavated 1972-1982 by CNRS and the University of Provence
A large Roman merchant ship that sank off the Giens peninsula near Hyères between 75 and 60 BCE with about 6,000 wine amphorae from Lazio. It is one of the largest Roman ships found.
A Roman wine freighter sinks off Giens with 6,000 amphorae
found by Greek sponge divers; salvaged 1900-1901 with the Greek Navy; new dives since 2014
A Roman-era cargo ship that sank off Antikythera around 65 BCE with bronze and marble statues and luxury goods. It held the Antikythera mechanism, often called the oldest known analogue computer.
Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution; Greek Ephorate of Underwater Antiquities
A Roman-era treasure ship sinks off Antikythera
Sponge divers find the Antikythera wreck
found by local fishermen; cargo in the Asian Civilisations Museum, Singapore

An Arab sewn-plank dhow that sank off Belitung, Indonesia, around 830 CE with about 60,000 Tang dynasty ceramics and gold and silver. It is direct evidence of 9th-century sea trade between China and the Middle East.
An Arab dhow sinks off Belitung with 60,000 pieces of Tang china
excavated in a cofferdam in 1962; now in the Viking Ship Museum, Roskilde
Five Viking-age ships deliberately sunk in the 11th century to block a channel of Roskilde Fjord against attack from the sea. They range from a warship to cargo ships.
Danish Agency for Culture and Palaces; Viking Ship Museum
Vikings sink five ships to block Roskilde Fjord
found in 1987; raised whole in a steel caisson in 2007; now in the Maritime Silk Road Museum, Yangjiang
A Southern Song dynasty merchant junk that sank off western Guangdong with porcelain, coins and metal goods. Raised whole in 2007, it has yielded over 180,000 objects.
A Song dynasty junk sinks off Guangdong (Nanhai One)
Nanhai One, a whole Song dynasty ship, is raised from the sea
found in the tidal mud of Houzhu harbour; excavated 1974; now in the Quanzhou Maritime Museum

A 13th-century Song dynasty ocean-going junk found in the mud of Houzhu harbour, Quanzhou, with spices and aromatic woods from Southeast Asia. It is physical evidence of Song shipbuilding and Quanzhou's overseas trade.
hull No. 1 confirmed 2011, No. 2 found 2015 (University of the Ryukyus); a National Historic Site of Japan

Ships of Kublai Khan's second invasion fleet were wrecked in Imari Bay off Takashima when a typhoon (the "kamikaze") struck in 1281. The wrecks are physical evidence of one of the largest seaborne invasions before modern times.
A typhoon wrecks Kublai Khan's invasion fleet off Takashima
Divers confirm a Mongol invasion ship off Takashima
ceramics netted by a fisherman in 1975; excavated 1976-1984; now at the National Maritime Museum, Mokpo

A Chinese Yuan dynasty trading ship bound for Japan that sank off Sinan, Korea, in 1323 with over 20,000 ceramics and about 28 tons of Chinese coins. Its excavation began underwater archaeology in South Korea.
A Yuan dynasty trader bound for Japan sinks off Sinan, Korea
A fisherman nets Yuan dynasty china: the Sinan wreck is found
identified as a medieval warship in 2000; excavated by Blekinge Museum and Södertörn University
Flagship of King Hans of Denmark-Norway, which caught fire and sank at anchor off Ronneby in June 1495 while the king was ashore. It is the best-preserved late-medieval warship found.
Blekinge Museum; PLOS ONE (Foley et al.)
King Hans's flagship Gribshunden burns and sinks off Ronneby
located in 1971; raised 11 October 1982; now in the Mary Rose Museum, Portsmouth
Henry VIII's warship heeled over and sank in the Solent during a battle with a French fleet. Raised in 1982, it is a Tudor time capsule of about 19,000 objects.
Henry VIII's warship Mary Rose sinks in the Solent
The Mary Rose is raised from the Solent
found in 2011 by Ocean Discovery with side-scan sonar
The Swedish flagship of Eric XIV, one of the largest warships of its day, caught fire and exploded in the first Battle of Öland against a Danish-Lübeck fleet. The wreck is unusually well preserved.
The Swedish warship Mars explodes off Öland
Divers find the warship Mars off Öland
found 1967 by Robert Sténuit's team; treasure in the Ulster Museum, Belfast
A galleass of the Spanish Armada, overloaded with survivors of other wrecks, that struck Lacada Point on the Antrim coast in a storm. It was the Armada's heaviest loss of life.
The Armada galleass Girona is wrecked on the Antrim coast
found by diver Edmund Downing in 1958

Flagship of a relief fleet for Jamestown, deliberately run onto a reef off Bermuda in a hurricane in July 1609; everyone aboard reached shore. The survivors began the English settlement of Bermuda, and the wreck is thought to have inspired The Tempest.
The Sea Venture is run onto Bermuda's reefs in a hurricane
main cargo found 20 July 1985 by Mel Fisher's Treasure Salvors after a 16-year search
A Spanish treasure galleon of the 1622 fleet, wrecked by a hurricane on reefs west of Key West. Its silver, gold and emeralds made it one of the most valuable wrecks ever recovered.
A hurricane sinks the treasure galleon Atocha off the Florida Keys
The Atocha's silver is found off Key West
found by Anders Franzén in 1956; raised 24 April 1961; now in the Vasa Museum, Stockholm
A Swedish royal warship that capsized in Stockholm harbour on her maiden voyage because she was top-heavy. Raised almost intact in 1961, she is the best-preserved 17th-century ship in the world.
The warship Vasa capsizes on her maiden voyage in Stockholm
The Vasa is raised almost whole from Stockholm harbour
about 40 in the wreck; about 110 to 125 later killed by mutineers
found on Morning Reef in 1963; hull in the WA Shipwrecks Museum, Fremantle

A Dutch East India Company ship wrecked on Morning Reef in the Houtman Abrolhos on her maiden voyage. Many survivors were later killed by a group of mutineers; her hull is the only early-17th-century VOC hull studied in detail.
The Dutch ship Batavia is wrecked in the Houtman Abrolhos
The Batavia wreck is found off Western Australia
found by Anders Franzén in 1980; Kalmar County Museum holds over 30,000 finds
One of the largest warships of her time, the Swedish flagship capsized and exploded at the Battle of Öland against a Danish-Dutch fleet.
The Swedish warship Kronan is found off Öland
found 1995 by the Texas Historical Commission; now in the Bullock Texas State History Museum
A ship of La Salle's expedition to found a French colony on the Gulf of Mexico, which ran aground in a storm in Matagorda Bay, Texas. The whole hull and over a million artefacts were recovered.
La Salle's ship La Belle runs aground in Matagorda Bay
La Salle's ship La Belle is found in Matagorda Bay
HMS Association found in 1967 by Royal Navy divers; wreckage 10-40 m deep

Four Royal Navy ships under Admiral Sir Cloudesley Shovell, including the flagship Association, were wrecked on the Isles of Scilly after a navigation error (22 October in the old Julian calendar). It helped lead to the Longitude Act of 1714.
Four Royal Navy ships are wrecked on the Isles of Scilly
found in 2015 by the Colombian Navy with WHOI; the exact site is kept secret
A Spanish treasure galleon sunk in a battle with a British squadron off Cartagena, carrying gold, silver and emeralds. It is among the most valuable wrecks known.
The treasure galleon San José sinks off Cartagena
Colombia's navy finds the San José galleon
found by Barry Clifford in 1984; identified by the ship's bell in 1985
A former slave ship captured by the pirate Samuel Bellamy, wrecked in a nor'easter off Wellfleet, Cape Cod. It is the only fully authenticated Golden Age pirate shipwreck.
Massachusetts Office of Coastal Zone Management
The pirate ship Whydah is wrecked off Cape Cod
The pirate wreck Whydah is found off Cape Cod
found 21 November 1996; studied by the North Carolina Department of Natural and Cultural Resources
Blackbeard's flagship, a former French slave ship, ran aground off Beaufort Inlet, North Carolina, and was abandoned. Its excavation gives a rare physical record of early-18th-century piracy.
North Carolina Department of Natural and Cultural Resources
Blackbeard's Queen Anne's Revenge runs aground off North Carolina
Blackbeard's flagship is found off Beaufort Inlet
found by Odyssey Marine Exploration in 2008; now owned by the Maritime Heritage Foundation
A 100-gun first-rate and Admiral Balchin's flagship, lost with all hands in a Channel storm. Until the wreck was found it was thought to have struck the Casquets off Alderney.
HMS Victory, a 100-gun flagship, is lost with all hands in the Channel
The 1744 HMS Victory is found far from where she was thought lost
remains in Bounty Bay rediscovered by Luis Marden in 1957
The Royal Navy ship taken in the 1789 mutiny was run aground, stripped and burned by the mutineers at Pitcairn Island. Ballast and cannon still lie in the surf of Bounty Bay.
The Bounty mutineers burn their ship at Pitcairn
found 2 September 2014 by Parks Canada, guided partly by Inuit knowledge
Flagship of Franklin's 1845 Northwest Passage expedition, abandoned in the ice in April 1848; no one survived the expedition. The wreck is a National Historic Site managed with Inuit.
Franklin's ships Erebus and Terror are abandoned in the Arctic ice
found 3 September 2016 in Terror Bay on a tip from Inuk hunter Sammy Kogvik
The second ship of Franklin's lost expedition, abandoned with Erebus in 1848. She lies largely intact 21 to 24 m deep in Terror Bay, King William Island.
HMS Terror is found in Terror Bay
site known since the wreck; excavated 1986-88

A Royal Navy iron paddle troopship that struck a rock off Danger Point, South Africa. The soldiers stood fast so that women and children could take the boats, the origin of the "women and children first" Birkenhead drill.
The troopship Birkenhead sinks off Danger Point: women and children first
rediscovered by the Irish Sub-Aqua Club in 1959
A new iron clipper carrying emigrants from Liverpool to Australia, wrecked on Lambay Island off Dublin two days into her maiden voyage. Faulty compasses contributed.
The emigrant clipper Tayleur is wrecked on Lambay Island
salvaged soon after; remains lie in shallow water off Moelfre, Anglesey
A steam clipper returning from Melbourne with gold, driven onto rocks off Anglesey in the Royal Charter Storm. The loss led to the first public storm-warning service.
Royal Commission on the Ancient and Historical Monuments of Wales; University of Liverpool
The Royal Charter is wrecked off Anglesey in a great storm
found 27 August 1973 by a Duke University team; the first US National Marine Sanctuary (1975)
The Union ironclad that fought CSS Virginia at Hampton Roads foundered in a storm off Cape Hatteras while under tow. Her turret was raised in 2002.
The ironclad USS Monitor founders off Cape Hatteras
The wreck of USS Monitor is found off Cape Hatteras
located 1995; raised 8 August 2000; at the Warren Lasch Conservation Center
A Confederate hand-cranked submarine that became the first submarine to sink an enemy warship, USS Housatonic, off Charleston, then sank with all eight crew.
The submarine H. L. Hunley sinks a warship, then is lost
The Hunley submarine is found off Charleston
probable remains found in 1982 under a field on the Arkansas side; the river has moved
An overloaded Mississippi steamboat carrying paroled Union prisoners of war, whose boilers exploded near Memphis. It is the deadliest maritime disaster in US history.
Encyclopedia of Arkansas (Central Arkansas Library System)
The steamboat Sultana explodes on the Mississippi
A Thames pleasure paddle steamer cut in two by the collier Bywell Castle at Gallions Reach. Most victims drowned in water polluted by sewage outfalls; it is the Thames's worst disaster.
The Princess Alice sinks in the Thames
beached burning at North Brother Island
An excursion steamboat chartered by a German-American church group caught fire on New York's East River; its life preservers were rotten. It was New York City's deadliest disaster before 2001.
The General Slocum burns on New York's East River
A Danish emigrant liner bound for New York that struck Hasselwood Rock beside Rockall and sank. It was the worst civilian transatlantic disaster before the Titanic.
The emigrant ship Norge sinks at Rockall
found 1 September 1985 by a WHOI and IFREMER expedition led by Robert Ballard and Jean-Louis Michel
The White Star liner sank on her maiden voyage after hitting an iceberg. The wreck lies in two main pieces about 350 nautical miles off Newfoundland and is protected under a US-UK agreement.
The wreck of the Titanic is found
located by divers in 1964; National Historic Site of Canada since 2009
A Canadian Pacific liner that sank in about 14 minutes in the St. Lawrence after a collision with the collier Storstad in fog. It is Canada's worst maritime disaster.
Parks Canada register; Fisheries and Oceans Canada
The Empress of Ireland sinks in the St. Lawrence
first located in 1935; protected by an Irish Underwater Heritage Order
A Cunard liner torpedoed by U-20 off the Old Head of Kinsale, sinking in 18 minutes. The deaths of 128 Americans helped turn US opinion against Germany.
Geological Survey Ireland (INFOMAR); Library of Congress
A U-boat sinks the liner Lusitania off Ireland
An overloaded, top-heavy excursion steamer chartered for a company picnic rolled over at its dock in the Chicago River. It is Chicago's deadliest disaster.
Chicago Public Library; US Navy NHHC
The Eastland rolls over in the Chicago River
found 5 March 2022 by the Endurance22 expedition
Shackleton's ship was crushed by pack ice in the Weddell Sea; all 28 men survived. The wreck is a protected Antarctic Treaty historic site.
Falklands Maritime Heritage Trust; Journal of Navigation
The ice crushes Shackleton's Endurance, which sinks in the Weddell Sea
Shackleton's Endurance is found 3,000 m down
Titanic's younger sister, serving as a hospital ship, struck a mine off Kea and sank in under an hour. She is the largest passenger-ship wreck on the seabed.
The hospital ship Britannic sinks off Kea
most ships salvaged in the 1920s-30s; three battleships remain as scheduled monuments
Interned German crews scuttled 52 of 74 ships of the High Seas Fleet to keep them from being handed over under the peace treaty. It was the largest single loss of shipping in history.
Scuttling of the German fleet at Scapa Flow
protected by France as a war grave
A British liner serving as a troopship, bombed off Saint-Nazaire while evacuating troops and civilians from France. It is the largest loss of life on a single British ship.
The troopship Lancastria is sunk off Saint-Nazaire
found by David Mearns's team in 2001
Royal Navy battlecruiser sunk by Bismarck in the Battle of the Denmark Strait after a magazine explosion.
The wreck of HMS Hood is found
found by Robert Ballard's team in 1989
German battleship disabled by British ships and aircraft three days after sinking HMS Hood, then scuttled.
US battleship destroyed at Pearl Harbor when a bomb set off its forward magazine. Its dead are about half of the Americans killed that day, and the wreck remains their resting place.
US Navy NHHC; National Park Service
protected war grave off Łeba, Poland
A German liner carrying refugees and military personnel west from East Prussia, torpedoed by the Soviet submarine S-13. It is regarded as the deadliest single-ship sinking in history.
The Wilhelm Gustloff is torpedoed in the Baltic with thousands of refugees
located by a Japanese expedition in 1985
The largest battleship ever built, sunk by US carrier aircraft during Operation Ten-Go on a one-way mission toward Okinawa.
The wreck of the battleship Yamato is found
found by Paul Allen's R/V Petrel team in August 2017
US heavy cruiser that had just delivered atomic bomb components to Tinian, torpedoed by the Japanese submarine I-58. It sank in 12 minutes and survivors spent four to five days in the water.
The cruiser Indianapolis is torpedoed in the Philippine Sea
USS Indianapolis is found 5,500 m down
raised in 1956 and returned to service
A Chinese passenger steamer, overloaded with people fleeing the civil war, sank near the mouth of the Huangpu River after an explosion, probably a leftover wartime mine.
The overloaded steamer Kiangya sinks off Shanghai
Italian liner that sank off Nantucket after colliding in fog with the MS Stockholm. Most of the 1,660 aboard were rescued; the collision led to better radar training and ship-to-ship radio rules.
The liner Andrea Doria sinks off Nantucket after a collision in fog
A US nuclear attack submarine lost during deep-diving tests east of Cape Cod. It led to the Navy's SUBSAFE program; no SUBSAFE-certified submarine has been lost since.
The nuclear submarine Thresher is lost on a test dive
about 119,000 tonnes of crude oil spilled
A supertanker that ran aground on the Seven Stones reef between Cornwall and Scilly. The UK's first major tanker spill led to international oil spill liability rules and the founding of ITOPF.
The tanker Torrey Canyon spills 119,000 tonnes of oil off Cornwall
located days later by a US Navy aircraft
A Great Lakes ore freighter that sank suddenly in a storm on Lake Superior with no distress call. Its loss led to depth finders, survival suits and annual Coast Guard pre-season inspections.
The Edmund Fitzgerald sinks in a Lake Superior storm
about 223,000 tonnes of crude oil plus 4,000 tonnes of fuel spilled

A supertanker that ran aground on the Portsall rocks in Brittany after a steering failure, spilling its whole cargo. France responded with a shipping lane scheme off Ushant and the Cedre response centre.
The Amoco Cadiz spills 223,000 tonnes of oil in Brittany
refloated and scuttled at Matauri Bay in 1987
The Greenpeace ship was sunk at Marsden Wharf, Auckland, by bombs planted by French intelligence agents ahead of protests against nuclear testing; photographer Fernando Pereira was killed.
NZ Ministry for Culture and Heritage
The Rainbow Warrior is bombed in Auckland harbour

A roll-on/roll-off ferry that capsized just outside Zeebrugge after leaving with its bow doors open. It led to bow-door indicators, stricter ferry stability rules and the UK Marine Accident Investigation Branch.
The ferry Herald of Free Enterprise capsizes off Zeebrugge

An overcrowded Philippine ferry that collided with the tanker MT Vector in the Tablas Strait off Mindoro; the burning cargo engulfed both ships. It is the deadliest peacetime maritime disaster on record.
The ferry Doña Paz sinks in the Tablas Strait after a collision
about 11 million US gallons of crude oil spilled
An oil tanker that ran aground on Bligh Reef in Prince William Sound, Alaska. It led to the US Oil Pollution Act of 1990.
NOAA Office of Response and Restoration
The Exxon Valdez runs aground and spills oil in Alaska
protected as a grave site by the 1995 Estonia Agreement
A Tallinn to Stockholm ferry that sank in a storm after its bow visor failed and the car deck flooded. It led to stricter SOLAS stability and evacuation rules for passenger ships.
The ferry Estonia sinks in a Baltic storm
A Russian nuclear-powered submarine sunk in the Barents Sea by torpedo explosions during a naval exercise; all 118 aboard died.
The submarine Kursk sinks in the Barents Sea
A Senegalese government ferry between Ziguinchor and Dakar that capsized in a storm off The Gambia while carrying more than three times its capacity.
Université Cheikh Anta Diop; American Geographical Society
The ferry Le Joola capsizes off The Gambia
about 64,000 tonnes of heavy fuel oil spilled
A single-hull tanker that broke in two and sank off Galicia after storm damage. The spill fouled about 2,900 km of coast in Spain, France and Portugal.
The tanker Prestige breaks apart off Galicia
righted in 2013, refloated and towed to Genoa in 2014
A cruise ship that hit rocks and capsized off Isola del Giglio after sailing too close to shore. It led to rules requiring passenger muster drills before departure.
The Costa Concordia capsizes off Giglio
A South Korean ferry that capsized off Jindo while overloaded with poorly secured cargo. Most of the dead were high school students on a school trip.
The ferry Sewol capsizes off Jindo
